title: White Sox likely to place Munetaka Murakami on IL, call up Jacob Gonzalez: Sources
content:
The Chicago White Sox will be without Munetaka Murakami, the American League’s co-home run leader, for at least a couple of weeks. Murakami injured a hamstring running out a grounder in the third inning of Friday’s 4-3 win over the Detroit Tigers, according to team sources who said the club will call up Jacob Gonzalez. The injury will likely land Murakami on the injured list.

Murakami, who blasted 56 homers for the Yakult Swallows in Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball Organization in 2022, has been a revelation since joining the White Sox. He has been a three-true-outcomes hitter, with 20 home runs, 44 walks (fifth in baseball) and 80 strikeouts (tied for third). He’s third on the White Sox in bWAR at 1.9 as the South Siders have been one of the season’s biggest surprises, with a 30-27 record that has placed them second in the AL Central.

Gonzalez gets the call-up after hitting his 19th home run Friday for Triple-A Charlotte. That total, along with his 62 RBIs, leads the International League.
